Demystifying the underlying mathematics that power everything from basic linear regression to billion-parameter Large Language Models.

Photo by Growtika on UnsplashWhat if I told you that every machine learning model in existence — whether it’s a simple trend line predicting housing prices or a massive neural network generating human-like text — is fundamentally trying to solve the exact same mathematical problem?
Behind the buzzwords of “Artificial Intelligence,” “training,” and “optimization,” there isn’t a machine actually learning in the human sense. There is only a compute unit executing a central, overarching mathematical task: estimating an unknown probability density from a limited set of samples.
Whether we are trying to find the joint probability P(x, y), the conditional probability P(y|x), or the marginal probability P(x), the interpretation of our problem changes, but the core mathematical challenge remains identical.
Here is the unvarnished, technical breakdown of that central challenge, the three-step recipe used to solve it, and why this exact framework might be the brute-force path to Artificial General Intelligence (AGI).
